title: What Are You Rehearsing?
headline: How Replaying Hurt Shapes What You Believe
tagline: The original event may have lasted five minutes. Rehearsal can give it five years of influence.
seo_title: How Replaying Hurt Shapes You: Philippians 4:8 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: One painful moment shouldn't write a theology about everybody. A devotional for men on rumination, generalizing hurt and Philippians 4:8.
verse_text: ….whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable….think about such things.

scriptures.text: ….whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable….think about such things.
….whose delight is in the law of the LORD, and who meditates on his law day and night.

items: The conversation ended three hours ago.
They aren’t beside you at 2:00 AM.
But you’re replaying what they said.

blocks.text: The original event may have lasted five minutes. Rehearsal can give it five years of influence.

items: But there is a difference between processing…. and rehearsing a verdict.
Rehearsal: “I can’t believe they did that.” Again. Again.
Then someone new enters your life.
But they’re entering a story already written by someone else.
That’s how yesterday can start interpreting tomorrow.

sections.label: One Painful Moment Should Not Write a Theology

items: One church wounded you: “Church is fake.”
History is formative. History is not sovereign.
Biblical meditation is deliberate rehearsal of truth in a world constantly rehearsing rival interpretations.
The time to furnish the mind with truth is before the storm asks the mind for an interpretation.
Don’t only starve the lie. Feed the truth.
Fear does not get final authorship.
